Question words: ما, من, أين, هل
My, your, his, her: possessive endings

decks.name: Letters 1: alif to sad
decks.desc: The first 14 letters, alif to ṣād, with their sounds and families.

decks.name: Letters 2: dad to ya
decks.desc: The last 14 letters, ḍād to yāʾ.

decks.name: Vowels and marks
decks.desc: Short and long vowels, sukun, shadda, tanwin, hamza, ة, ى, and ال with sun and moon letters.

decks.name: Sound pairs
decks.desc: Words that differ only in a sound English speakers merge: q / k, ṣ / s, ṭ / t, ʿ / ʾ, ḥ / h, kh / ḥ, short / long, single / doubled.

decks.name: Greetings and courtesy
decks.desc: Hello, thank you, please, sorry, goodbye: the phrases MSA shares with everyday speech.

decks.name: About me
decks.desc: Your name, where you're from, where you live, what you do.

decks.name: Family and people
decks.desc: Family members and people, with my / your.

decks.name: Numbers and money
decks.desc: Numbers 0–100, the Eastern Arabic digits, prices and currencies.

decks.name: Food and drink
decks.desc: Coffee, tea, food, ordering and paying.

decks.name: Home and things
decks.desc: Rooms and everyday objects; "I have"; the and a.

decks.name: Describing things
decks.desc: Adjectives in pairs, with agreement.

decks.name: Daily routine
decks.desc: Everyday verbs in the present, and word families.

decks.name: Time and days
decks.desc: Today, tomorrow, yesterday, days of the week, and the past.

decks.name: Around town and directions
decks.desc: Asking the way: where, right, left, near, far.

decks.name: Travel and help
decks.desc: Airport, hotel, transport, and asking for help.

decks.name: Spoken Arabic
decks.desc: The MSA word, and what you'll hear instead in Egypt and the Levant (recognition only).

decks.name: Traps for English speakers
decks.desc: Calques, false friends and courtesy traps.

decks.name: Compliments
decks.desc: Everyday praise: food and the cook, work and effort, someone's home, the learner's Arabic, and how people answer (with the blessing phrases).

decks.name: Flirting
decks.desc: Words people flirt with, the phrases built from them, then moves and replies, including kind ways to say no. Mostly indirect, as in real life.

decks.name: Top nouns
decks.desc: The most-used nouns, with gender and the plural where it changes inside.

decks.name: Top verbs
decks.desc: The most-used verbs by their past "he" form, with the "I" form of the present.

decks.name: Top adjectives
decks.desc: The most-used adjectives, with the feminine form.

decks.name: Top adverbs
decks.desc: Time, place, manner and degree: very, only, also, maybe, soon.

decks.name: Top pronouns
decks.desc: I, you, he, she, the possessive endings, this and that, and some, every, nobody.

decks.name: Top prepositions
decks.desc: In, from, to, with, before, after, and the forms with endings: for me, with you, I have.

decks.name: Top conjunctions
decks.desc: And, or, but, because, if, when, that, so.

decks.name: Top interjections
decks.desc: What people really exclaim: oh, ouch, wow, congratulations, oh my God.

decks.name: Top words
decks.desc: Small words that fit no other class: no, will, did not, numbers to twenty, ordinals, days.
